Kidmore Road.road: Fairly wide two-way road, no centre line on most stretches, dashed give-way lines at junctions, kerbside parking, no humps seen.
Kidmore Road.note: Long leafy road of big Edwardian and interwar red-brick detached and semi houses, many with white-rendered or mock-Tudor gables; deep front gardens behind hedges and low red-brick walls, tall trees and grass verges at the north end.

Albert Road.road: Two-way residential road, no centre line, dashed give-way at junctions, on-street parking, grass verges in places, no humps seen.
Albert Road.note: Edwardian red-brick detached and semi houses with steep gables, some with white-rendered or mock-Tudor upper gables and buff-brick dressings; a modern red-brick flats block at the south end; thick hedges and low brick walls in front, trees and a green at the north end.

St Peter's Avenue.road: Two-way residential road without centre line, grass verges with trees at the south end, kerbside parking; the southern end views actually look onto the A4074 (Peppard Road) with a flint/stone retaining wall.
St Peter's Avenue.note: Leafy road of detached houses largely hidden by tall hedges and trees: interwar and 1960s-80s red and orange brick houses, some bungalows with brown concrete tile roofs, a few white-rendered upper floors; low brick walls, fences and hedges in front.

Highmoor Road.road: Two-way road, no centre line, double yellow lines near junctions, white give-way triangles and dashed lines at the Albert Road junction, kerb parking elsewhere.
Highmoor Road.note: Interwar red-brick detached and semi houses with hipped dark-tile roofs, some white-rendered bays, plus a red-brick church hall and small modern flats block at the west end; tall hedges and close-board fences on low red-brick walls hide many fronts.

Buxton Avenue.road: Fairly narrow residential road, no centre line, cars parked on street and in front drives; double yellow lines at the junctions.
Buxton Avenue.note: Edwardian/interwar red-brick detached and semi houses with steep front gables, white-rendered or tile-hung upper floors and some mock-Tudor gables; low red-brick walls, a few fences and hedges in front.

Shepherds Lane.road: Wide busy road with a white centre line, broad grass verges on both sides and a pavement; give-way at the junctions.
Shepherds Lane.note: Wide verged road of detached houses and bungalows set well back behind tall hedges, fences and conifers, mostly hidden; a 1960s-70s white-balconied house and a mock-Tudor mews group visible among them.

Carlton Road.road: Quiet estate road, no centre line, grass verges and pavements, cars on drives and kerbside.
Carlton Road.note: 1960s-70s estate: semis with steep catslide gables clad in dark grey-green weatherboarding over white render, plus later brick detached houses with gables; open-plan lawns and block-paved drives.

Aberaman.road: Narrow cul-de-sac estate road, no markings, no through traffic, cars on drives.
Aberaman.note: 1990s-2000s executive estate of red-brick detached houses with dark tile roofs, brick bands and chimneys, small mock-Tudor gable details and porch canopies; open lawns, some hedges and high brick garden walls with dark bands, mature trees around.

Hunters Chase.road: Winding estate road, no centre line, give-way lines at the junctions, pavement one or both sides; cars on drives.
Hunters Chase.note: 1980s-90s estate road of red-brick detached houses with dark concrete-tile roofs and chimneys, largely screened from the road by tall hedges, close-board fences and brick garden walls; mature trees.

Hewett Avenue.road: Narrow lane-like road, no centre line or markings, grass verges, pavement on one side; very green and rural feel at the north end.
Hewett Avenue.note: Semi-rural lane with houses largely hidden behind tall hedges and trees; the visible ones are 1950s-60s brick bungalows with dormers and plain semis in pale mixed brick with brown-tile roofs and open lawns.

Gurney Close.road: Quiet cul-de-sac, no markings, pavements both sides, a turning head; cars on drives.
Gurney Close.note: 1960s-70s close of red/orange-brick bungalows and chalet bungalows (some with dormers) under dark brown concrete-tile roofs, set behind low brick walls with small lawns; tall hedges and fences at the entrance.

Tredegar Road.road: Hilly winding estate distributor road with a white centre line in places, double yellows at the junctions, pavements; woodland banks and a steel railing along parts.
Tredegar Road.note: Steep hillside 1980s estate road: stepped terraces of red/buff-brick town houses with gables, red-brick detached houses and a few bungalows, separated by long stretches of wooded bank and verge with no houses.

Woodford Close.road: Quiet curving cul-de-sac, no markings, pavements, cars on drives; wooded bank at the entrance.
Woodford Close.note: 1960s-70s close of buff/yellow-brick link-detached houses with low-pitch brown-tile roofs, white weatherboard or tile-hung panels and porch canopies, set on open-plan lawns among mature trees.

Darell Road.road: Residential road, no centre line, give-way white lines at junctions, cars parked kerbside; pavements both sides.
Darell Road.note: Large late-Victorian/Edwardian villas in red and grey Reading brick with steep gables, bay windows and some mock-Tudor or rendered gables, behind low red-brick walls topped with tall hedges and timber gates; big pines and mature trees.

Knowle Close.road: Quiet cul-de-sac, no markings except double yellows at the mouth; wide grass corners, cars on drives.
Knowle Close.note: 1950s-60s close of large red-brick detached bungalows with long hipped dark-tile roofs, chimneys and attached garages, on open lawns and wide drives, framed by tall hedges and mature trees.

Queensborough Drive.road: Quiet estate road, no markings, pavements, block-paved drives; cars on drives and kerbside.
Queensborough Drive.note: 1970s detached estate houses in red/orange brick, about half with white weatherboarded upper floors, integral garages and porch canopies; open-plan lawns and wide drives, conifers and mature trees.

Tyler Close.road: Quiet close, no markings, pavements, cars kerbside and on drives.
Tyler Close.note: Only two views, mostly of garages and side walls: 1960s-70s estate with buff-brick garages, red-brick houses with weatherboarded fronts, low brick walls with pierced concrete screen blocks; fences and trees.

Hilltop Road.road: Residential road, no centre line, grass verges, cars on drives and kerbside; ends in a small turning head.
Hilltop Road.note: 1950s-60s red-brick semis with tiled porch canopies and brown concrete-tile roofs along grass verges, plus a 1980s cul-de-sac end of red-brick detached houses with integral garages; low fences and open lawns.

Orwell Close.road: Quiet cul-de-sac, no markings, pavement, cars on drives.
Orwell Close.note: 1960s-70s close of plain red-brick detached houses with low-pitch dark-tile roofs, chimneys, tiled porch canopies and attached garages on open-plan lawns; big trees behind.

Dellwood Park.road: Private-feel winding cul-de-sac, no markings, narrow pavement or none; brick gate piers at the entrance.
Dellwood Park.note: 1990s-2000s executive cul-de-sac of large red-brick detached houses with steep gables, mock-Tudor black-and-white upper storeys or a cream-rendered gable, dark tile roofs; brick gate piers, hedges, railings and mature conifers.

Blagrave Farm Lane.road: Narrow unmarked country lane, no pavement, overgrown hedgerow verges.
Blagrave Farm Lane.note: Rural lane with dense hedgerow and trees; the only houses seen are a white-rendered interwar chalet house with a tall chimney and a mock-Tudor gabled house behind close-board fences. The western panorama has no Street View imagery.

Haldane Road.road: Unmarked residential road with a junction bell-mouth, pavements, cars on drives and kerbside.
Haldane Road.note: Mostly 1950s-60s bungalows and chalet bungalows, red brick or white render with hipped dark-tile roofs, behind low brick walls, close-board fences and hedges; a few two-storey houses.

Balliol Road.road: Quiet unmarked residential road with bends, pavements, cars on drives.
Balliol Road.note: Mixed 1930s-1980s houses: red-brick semis with hipped dark-tile roofs, a large red-brick detached house with tile-hung gable, a white-rendered house and a brick bungalow; white picket fences, tall conifer hedges and lawns.

Kelvedon Way.road: Quiet unmarked estate road, pavements, give-way markings at the junction, cars kerbside and on drives.
Kelvedon Way.note: 1960s estate of red-brick bungalows (detached and semi) with hipped dark/brown concrete-tile roofs, attached garages and low red-brick front walls, some with pierced screen-block tops; one cream-rendered bungalow.

Cwmcarn.road: Narrow cul-de-sac, no markings, block-paved drives, cars on drives.
Cwmcarn.note: 1990s executive estate of red-brick detached houses with steep front gables, many with black-and-white mock-Tudor upper gables, dark tile roofs, integral garages and block-paved drives on open lawns; woodland behind.

Graveney Drive.road: Narrow wooded cul-de-sac, no markings, overgrown flint/stone retaining wall at the entrance, cars on drives.
Graveney Drive.note: Short 1960s-70s cul-de-sac of detached houses, red brick with some white-rendered upper floors and plain gables, on open lawns; the entrance is heavily wooded with an old stone wall, so few houses are visible.

Church Road.road: Busy hilly through road with a white centre line, hatched markings and turn lanes at the junction, double yellow lines, pavements; tall flint-and-brick retaining walls.
Church Road.note: Hill road by St Peter s church: Georgian/Victorian red-brick houses with slate roofs and stone dressings, a mock-Tudor Edwardian house, a 1960s three-storey red-brick flat block, all behind old flint-and-brick walls, railings and thick hedges and trees.

Symeon Place.road: Private-looking 2000s cul-de-sac, no markings, block-paved bays, brick carport block.
Symeon Place.note: 2000s development of three-storey red-brick flat blocks and town houses with cream-rendered ground floors, small balconies, dark tile roofs and a brick carport, on open lawns with low hedges and big mature trees (copper beech).

Tylorstown.road: Hilly estate cul-de-sac, no markings, pavement, grass verges, dense wooded bank opposite.
Tylorstown.note: 1990s hillside estate of red-brick detached houses with orange tile-hung upper floors, small dormers and gabled porches, dark tile roofs, on open lawns; dense trees on the other side.
